narrative:
# Weekly Multi-Asset Technology & Growth Watchlist Briefing

This week’s tape was defined by a sharp factor reversal back into high-beta software, applied AI, and select digital advertising platforms, even as a number of cyclical and defensive exposures in our watchlist sold off hard. Within our coverage universe of 184 names, the most notable features were the outsized surge in Sable Offshore Corp. in energy, pronounced strength across marketing technology and cloud infrastructure beneficiaries like Wix, The Trade Desk, and Samsara, and a simultaneous drawdown in several semiconductor and storage hardware names including Lumentum, SiTime, and Western Digital. The result is an increasingly bifurcated landscape where investors are paying up for perceived secular growth durability and AI adjacency, while fading more rate- and cycle-sensitive exposures in airlines, traditional industrials, and several consumer staples, against a backdrop of a quiet earnings calendar over the next two weeks and an increasingly data-dependent macro and rates narrative.

## Market Overview

From a top-down perspective, the week in our watchlist can be characterized as a continuation of the rotation back toward secular growth, especially software and applied AI, after a period in which hardware and more cyclical exposures had outperformed. The strongest confirmation comes from the software-oriented ETF proxy in our universe, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF, which advanced by 7.8% over the week and is now up 4.9% on a one-month basis, signaling a broad-based bid for software risk rather than a narrow, stock-specific squeeze. IGV’s performance aligned with double-digit weekly gains across many individual software names, including Datadog, ServiceNow, Workday, and multiple vertical-market specialists, reinforcing the idea that investors are rotating into the software complex as a primary vehicle for AI and automation exposure.

Within this context, the single most eye-catching move on the watchlist was Sable Offshore Corp., which rallied 74.2% over the week and 73.8% over the past month. SOC’s surge stands out not only because it vastly exceeds moves in any other energy or industrial name in the universe, but also because it occurs in a period when several other cyclicals were actually down on the week, including United Airlines, which declined 13.4%, and Freeport-McMoRan, which fell 12.8%. This divergence suggests that the market is treating SOC as a name with idiosyncratic catalysts—possibly corporate events, asset value realization, or positioning dynamics—rather than as a simple beta play on broader energy or commodity trends.

The second major theme was the strong bid in digital commerce, digital advertising, and marketing technology. Wix gained 33.2% on the week and 18.4% over the month, Shopify and GoDaddy each added 7.8% over the week with mid-teens to low-single-digit moves on the month, and The Trade Desk rallied 22.9% weekly with a 7.4% one-month gain. Complementing this, marketing automation and data platforms such as Klaviyo, Zeta Global, and LiveRamp delivered weekly gains of 20.5%, 11.2%, and 8.2% respectively, with all three also positive on a one-month basis. The breadth and magnitude of these moves indicate a robust re-rating in digital spend beneficiaries as the market leans into performance marketing, first-party data, and connected TV themes.

At the same time, several pockets of weakness highlight that this is not a uniform risk-on environment. Semiconductors and storage showed notable drawdowns, with Lumentum down 20.3%, SiTime down 17.7%, Sandisk down 17.0%, Onto Innovation down 16.8%, Teradyne down 14.7%, Seagate down 13.5%, and Western Digital down 12.3% on the week. Many of these names showed relatively muted or even positive one-month returns, indicating that the current week represents more of a sharp reversal or profit-taking after prior strength than a sustained downtrend. Meanwhile, data storage more broadly struggled, with Seagate and Western Digital both down double-digits on the week and negative on a one-month basis, while networking and optical names like Ciena also sold off sharply despite positive one-month performance.

The factor mix underneath these moves looks consistent with a market that is discriminating aggressively among AI and digital transformation narratives. Applied AI names such as Samsara and C3.ai were significant winners, with Samsara up 22.4% on the week and 40.9% on the month and C3.ai up 15.6% weekly despite being down 17.3% over the month. Data and analytics platforms like MongoDB, by contrast, saw a material derating, as MDB fell 17.7% on the week and 19.9% over the month, even while other observability and analytics peers, including Datadog and Dynatrace, posted solid gains. This divergence implies investors are rewarding AI stories with clear operating momentum and visible monetization while pushing back on names where the path from AI narrative to durable free cash flow remains less certain.

The macro overlay remains one of cautious optimism rather than outright euphoria. The strong performance of multiple cybersecurity and enterprise software leaders, with names like CrowdStrike, ServiceNow, Intuit, and Constellation Software all posting mid-teens weekly gains, speaks to an appetite for quality compounders, even as more defensive categories such as consumer staples and some healthcare names lagged. Several large-cap staples in our universe, including Clorox, Unilever, McCormick, and Constellation Brands, fell between roughly 7% and 10% on the week and are mostly flat to negative on a one-month basis. This pattern is consistent with a market incrementally moving away from defensive positioning toward growth and cyclicality, but still with a strong preference for high-quality, cash-generating software assets over more capital-intensive or commodity-sensitive exposures.

## Sector Leadership & Rotation

Sector leadership this week was dominated by software and digital platforms, especially within applied AI, cybersecurity, and marketing technology, while semiconductors, storage, and several cyclical and defensive groups underperformed. The sector-level snapshot from our subsector buckets underscores this dynamic clearly. In software infrastructure, Samsara’s 22.4% weekly gain and 40.9% monthly rise led the pack, supported by double-digit weekly gains from Palantir at 14.6%, Cloudflare at 13.4%, Datadog at 12.3%, and UiPath at 10.5%. This cluster of performance is notable not just for its magnitude but also for its concentration in names directly exposed to AI-enabled operations, observability, and automation, all of which are central to current enterprise spending priorities.

Application software also participated strongly in the rotation, with Intuit and Constellation Software each advancing 17.6% on the week, Guidewire up 16.2%, RingCentral up 15.3%, ServiceNow up 15.1%, ServiceTitan up 14.6%, Workday up 12.9%, and Manhattan Associates up 12.6%. Many of these names also showed double-digit gains over the trailing month, including Constellation Software at 19.3%, Guidewire at 27.8%, ServiceTitan at 29.1%, and Manhattan Associates at 10.1%. The consistent strength across horizontal and vertical application software suggests that investors are broadening out beyond just core infrastructure and AI platforms to incorporate more traditional workflow automation, ERP, and industry-specific solutions into their growth allocations.

Cybersecurity maintained its status as a secular winner with a defensive tilt, but this week’s behavior tilted more toward high-beta than low-volatility. CrowdStrike rose 15.3% on the week, Rapid7 rallied 13.7%, Zscaler gained 11.6%, Okta was up 11.3%, Palo Alto Networks increased 10.8%, Rubrik rose 10.0%, Tenable advanced 9.4%, and Check Point gained 8.7%. While not every name has positive one-month returns—Rapid7 is still down 36.0% over the month and Qualys remains under pressure on a one-month basis—investors clearly have an appetite to add or re-risk into cyber after prior drawdowns, particularly in platforms perceived as AI-enabled or offering broad cloud security capabilities.

Digital media and adtech provided another important source of leadership. The Trade Desk’s 22.9% weekly surge and 7.4% one-month advance came alongside a 16.8% weekly gain for Pinterest and 15.5% for AppLovin, as well as solid moves in Zeta Global, which rose 11.2%, LiveRamp, which gained 8.2%, Braze, which was up 6.1%, and Comcast, which added 3.1%. The breadth of this strength across demand-side platforms, social discovery, mobile app monetization, and CRM-style marketing software indicates that investors are increasingly convinced that digital ad spend is re-accelerating, supported by improved targeting, measurement, and the integration of AI into campaign optimization.

In contrast, semiconductor and related hardware names within our watchlist largely lagged as the market consolidated after prior outperformance and as investors appeared to scrutinize valuations and earnings durability more closely. Within the semiconductor bucket, Lumentum’s 20.3% weekly decline was the sharpest, but it followed a 20.0% gain over the month, suggesting that the current move may represent profit-taking or a reset after a strong run. SiTime fell 17.7% on the week and is down 5.9% over the month, Sandisk declined 17.0% weekly and 9.8% monthly, Onto Innovation was down 16.8% and 4.7% respectively, and Teradyne fell 14.7% on the week but remains modestly positive on a one-month basis. Storage names Seagate and Western Digital lost 13.5% and 12.3% on the week, respectively, and both are down high single to mid-teens percentages over the month, reinforcing that the current market tone is less constructive on traditional hardware even as AI-related semiconductor bellwethers like Marvell, which gained 9.7% on the week and 21.5% on the month, and Vertiv, which is modestly down on the week but up 32.4% on the month, continue to command premium interest.

The energy and industrials complex within the watchlist delivered a mixed picture. Sable Offshore’s 74.2% weekly explosion and Valero’s 9.8% gain contrast sharply with an 8.3% decline in Baker Hughes, a 13.4% drop in United Airlines, and a 12.8% selloff in Freeport-McMoRan. Within materials and mining, CF Industries rose 16.3% weekly and 22.3% monthly even as precious metals miners like Agnico Eagle and Newmont fell 12.2% and 10.6% respectively on the week. This divergence suggests investors are favoring nitrogen and agricultural-linked exposures over gold miners in the current environment, potentially reflecting nuanced views on fertilizer pricing, crop economics, and geopolitical supply dynamics, while airlines and some industrials such as Caterpillar, which was down 8.3% on the week, remain under pressure as investors reassess late-cycle risk.

Defensive sectors like consumer staples and parts of healthcare underperformed, underlining the rotation out of safety. Clorox declined 9.8% this week and is down 2.6% over the month, Unilever fell 9.4% weekly and 5.6% monthly, McCormick lost 8.7% and 2.6% over the same intervals, Constellation Brands dropped 7.2% weekly and 12.1% monthly, Mondelez fell 5.2% weekly and 1.7% monthly, and Keurig Dr Pepper was down 6.7% on the week and modestly down on the month. Healthcare services and devices also showed relative weakness, with Elevance Health down 9.5% weekly and 15.0% monthly, GE HealthCare down 11.9% and 10.1%, Medtronic down 6.9% and 10.7%, and Zoetis down 7.4% and 4.2%. Collectively, this pattern reinforces the view that the market is rotating away from low-volatility defensives toward higher-beta secular growth, albeit with an eye for quality and cash generation.

Finally, fintech performance was mixed but skewed positively toward higher-beta platforms leveraged to digital assets and consumer credit. Coinbase advanced 12.2% on the week and 17.0% over the month, Affirm gained 10.1% but remains down 16.8% on the month, and Shift4 Payments rose 8.6% despite a 17.8% one-month decline, while more traditional financials like Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Capital One saw modest weekly declines and small negative one-month returns. This suggests investors are expressing a preference for growthier, transaction-driven fintech exposure with optionality on crypto or consumer spending over more traditional, rate-sensitive financials.

## Top Movers & Earnings Recap

This week’s tape featured a long tail of mid-single to low-double-digit moves across the watchlist, but a handful of outsized winners and losers deserve special attention given their magnitude and potential signaling value. On the upside, Sable Offshore, Wix, The Trade Desk, Samsara, and Klaviyo form the core of the top-mover cohort, while on the downside, Lumentum, Corning, SiTime, MongoDB, Sandisk, Onto Innovation, Ciena, and several cyclical and consumer names represent the principal laggards.

Sable Offshore’s 74.2% weekly gain and roughly matching 73.8% one-month increase set it apart as the single most extreme mover in the universe. Within the energy and industrials bucket, the next best performer is Valero, up 9.8% on the week and 13.8% on the month, highlighting just how idiosyncratic SOC’s move is relative to peers. With no other watchlist energy or industrial name delivering anything remotely close in magnitude—California Resources, for instance, is up 10.0% on the week and 15.8% on the month—SOC’s behavior likely reflects stock-specific news, potential capital structure or asset developments, or a sharp short-covering dynamic. For portfolio construction, the move raises questions about position sizing, liquidity, and whether the stock’s risk-reward profile remains attractive after such a rapid repricing.

Wix’s 33.2% weekly gain and 18.4% one-month increase made it the standout in our consumer and digital commerce cohort, outpacing even high-beta names like Shopify and Sea. Shopify’s 7.8% weekly and 14.2% monthly gains are strong, but materially smaller in scale, while Sea actually declined 15.2% on the week and 13.4% over the month. The divergence between Wix and Sea underscores a market preference for asset-light, subscription- and SaaS-like business models with strong operating leverage, over more complex, capital-intensive e-commerce and gaming conglomerates exposed to emerging markets macro and regulatory risk. GoDaddy’s 7.8% gain on the week, despite a small 1.8% decline over the month, further supports the narrative that investors are willing to pay up for domain, hosting, and small-business web infrastructure as key beneficiaries of the online SMB economy.

The Trade Desk’s 22.9% weekly rally and 7.4% monthly climb anchor the digital advertising recovery story. Alongside TTD, Pinterest rose 16.8% over the week and 0.7% on the month, while AppLovin advanced 15.5% weekly and 29.6% monthly. The corresponding moves in Zeta Global, up 11.2% weekly and 8.5% monthly, and LiveRamp, up 8.2% weekly and 28.9% monthly, extend the rally into the broader performance marketing and data-activation ecosystem. Collectively, these gains suggest that investors have become increasingly constructive on the trajectory of digital ad budgets and the ability of platforms to maintain or expand margins in the face of privacy changes, signal loss, and an evolving regulatory environment.

Applied AI beneficiary Samsara posted a 22.4% weekly gain and a striking 40.9% rise over the month, confirming sustained momentum in demand for AI-enabled IoT, telematics, and operations analytics. C3.ai, another high-profile AI narrative, rose 15.6% this week but remains down 17.3% on the month, indicating that while short-term sentiment has improved, investors continue to differentiate between platforms based on visibility into enterprise adoption, recurring revenue growth, and unit economics. Within data and analytics, Palantir’s 14.6% weekly and 12.6% monthly gains contrast sharply with MongoDB’s 17.7% weekly and 19.9% monthly declines, underscoring this same pattern of differentiation. Datadog’s 12.3% weekly and 8.7% monthly increases and Dynatrace’s 9.3% weekly and 13.5% monthly gains reinforce the idea that observability platforms delivering both growth and profitability are being rewarded, while more purely growth-oriented, higher-valuation names such as MongoDB face greater scrutiny.

On the downside, Lumentum’s 20.3% weekly decline, despite a 20.0% rise over the past month, and Corning’s 18.0% weekly drop and 12.4% monthly gain are emblematic of volatile price action in hardware and optical names sensitive to both data center and telecom spending cycles. SiTime’s 17.7% weekly decline and negative 5.9% monthly move, alongside Onto Innovation’s 16.8% weekly decline and 4.7% monthly loss, suggest that investors are de-risking some more specialized semiconductor and test-equipment exposures even as broader AI semiconductor proxies remain relatively better bid. Seagate and Western Digital’s 13.5% and 12.3% weekly declines, combined with one-month losses of 15.7% and 9.0%, respectively, underscore continuing skepticism around the near-term trajectory of storage demand and pricing amid a somewhat uneven recovery.

Within networking, Ciena fell 15.6% on the week but remains up 16.0% over the month, indicating a sharp pullback after prior outperformance, possibly driven by profit-taking or reassessment of forward guidance and backlog quality. Meanwhile, Mohawk Industries’ 14.3% weekly and 17.7% monthly declines highlight sustained pressure in building products and residential-exposed names, as investors weigh mixed housing and renovation signals against elevated valuations and margin uncertainty. United Airlines’ 13.4% weekly and 15.9% monthly declines flag renewed concerns around travel demand, unit revenues, and cost inflation, further reinforcing the pattern of investors stepping back from cyclical, cost-intensive exposure in favor of capital-light digital and software assets.

The consumer staples and healthcare complexes saw multiple large negative movers without offsetting big winners, which is important for understanding factor rotation. Clorox fell 9.8% on the week and 2.6% on the month, Unilever dropped 9.4% and 5.6%, McCormick lost 8.7% and 2.6%, Constellation Brands fell 7.2% and 12.1%, Mondelez declined 5.2% and 1.7%, and Keurig Dr Pepper slipped 6.7% weekly and 0.7% monthly. On the healthcare side, Elevance’s 9.5% weekly and 15.0% monthly declines, GE HealthCare’s 11.9% and 10.1% declines, Medtronic’s 6.9% and 10.7% losses, and Zoetis’s 7.4% and 4.2% pullback collectively signal that defensive and income-oriented sectors are out of favor in this phase of the cycle, despite their fundamental stability.

From an earnings perspective, the calendar is notably light over the near term across our watchlist universe. There are no watchlist earnings scheduled over the next two weeks, which is unusual for such a broad coverage universe and effectively removes one of the key sources of idiosyncratic risk in the near term. In the absence of imminent earnings catalysts, price action is instead being driven by shifting macro expectations, factor flows, and company-specific news and positioning dynamics. This also means that the next major inflection in many of these names may not come until the next reporting season, placing greater emphasis on macro data, sector-level commentary, and alternative data signals in the interim.

## Macro & Rates Environment

The macro and rates backdrop for the week can best be characterized as a nuanced equilibrium where investors are increasingly data-dependent and highly sensitive to any shifts in the growth-versus-inflation trade-off, but without a single dominant macro shock driving cross-asset volatility. Within this environment, the equity market price action in our watchlist points toward a modestly more optimistic growth outlook relative to recent weeks, particularly as reflected in the strength of high-beta software, applied AI, and digital advertising names, and the concurrent derating of defensive consumer staples and some healthcare exposures.

The strong performance of software infrastructure and application software, as evidenced by IGV’s 7.8% weekly gain and 4.9% one-month move, suggests that investors are increasingly comfortable underwriting multi-year growth and free cash flow compounding in these sectors, despite continued macro uncertainty. The preference for secular growth is further reinforced by double-digit weekly gains in names like Intuit, ServiceNow, Constellation Software, CrowdStrike, and Datadog, all of which offer high recurring revenue, strong balance sheets, and exposure to AI and automation tailwinds. These are the kinds of assets investors tend to favor when they see a balanced macro risk profile where recession risks are not front-and-center but rates and policy direction still warrant caution.

At the same time, the sell-off in more cyclical and rate-sensitive sectors, including airlines, select industrials, and parts of materials, indicates persistent concerns about the durability of late-cycle growth. United Airlines’ 13.4% weekly decline and 15.9% monthly loss, alongside Caterpillar’s 8.3% weekly and 1.6% monthly decline and CNH Industrial’s 9.3% weekly and 6.8% monthly drop, suggest investors are either trimming cyclicals after prior strength or anticipating softer demand and margin pressure ahead. Similarly, the weakness in copper and mining proxy Freeport-McMoRan, down 12.8% on the week and 4.0% on the month, points to a more cautious view on industrial commodity demand relative to the more optimistic pricing of long-duration growth equities.

The performance of financials within the watchlist offers additional insight into how the market is reading the rates landscape. Fintech names leveraged to consumer spending and digital assets, such as Coinbase, Affirm, and Shift4 Payments, all posted strong weekly gains, with Coinbase up 12.2%, Affirm up 10.1%, and Shift4 up 8.6%, though Affirm and Shift4 remain down 16.8% and 17.8% respectively over the month. In contrast, more traditional financial institutions like Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Capital One faced modest weekly declines and small negative one-month returns. This split is consistent with a view that peak-rate fears may be easing, supporting risk-on behavior in higher-beta fintech, but that the overall rates environment remains challenging enough to weigh on net interest margins and balance-sheet-sensitive business models.

The underperformance of consumer staples and healthcare also fits a macro narrative where investors are less focused on immediate downside protection and more on capturing upside from secular growth and technological disruption. With Clorox, Unilever, McCormick, Constellation Brands, Mondelez, and Keurig Dr Pepper all registering meaningful weekly declines, and healthcare names like Elevance, GE HealthCare, and Medtronic similarly weak, the traditional playbook of rotating into defensives amid macro uncertainty appears to be on hold. Instead, investors are selectively using defensives as funding sources for renewed exposure to software, AI, and digital platforms.

Software and AI-linked infrastructure hardware’s mixed performance reflects the more complex interaction between macro, rates, and sector-specific fundamentals. On one hand, AI-levered data center and power infrastructure names like Marvell and Vertiv have continued to command investor attention, with Marvell up 9.7% weekly and 21.5% on the month and Vertiv down 5.1% on the week but up 32.4% on the month. On the other hand, more traditional hardware and networking plays like Lumentum, Corning, SiTime, Ciena, Seagate, and Western Digital have come under pressure. This suggests that investors are differentiating between AI infrastructure “picks and shovels” with clear near-term demand visibility and those with more cyclical or uncertain exposure to telecom, PC, or traditional enterprise spending cycles.

The absence of major upcoming earnings in the next two weeks also amplifies the role of macro and policy narratives in driving incremental price action. Without company-specific catalysts to reset expectations, names with strong momentum and clear secular narratives, such as Samsara, ServiceNow, and CrowdStrike, may continue to benefit from flows, while those with more ambiguous outlooks, including some of the weaker semiconductors and storage names, remain vulnerable to macro-driven risk-off episodes. In this environment, positioning, valuation discipline, and sensitivity to macro sentiment shifts become more important than near-term earnings revisions in explaining weekly moves.

## Watchlist Deep Dives

### Sable Offshore Corp. (SOC)

Sable Offshore delivered the single largest move in the watchlist this week, with its share price rising 74.2% over the week and 73.8% over the month. The magnitude and rapidity of this move suggest a combination of idiosyncratic catalysts, positioning dynamics, and possibly an element of short covering. From a sector perspective, SOC’s performance stands in stark contrast to the more modest moves in other energy names within our universe, such as Valero’s 9.8% weekly and 13.8% monthly gains and Baker Hughes’ 8.3% weekly decline and 1.1% monthly rise. This divergence makes it unlikely that broad-based sector fundamentals alone explain the rally.

For a buy-side portfolio, SOC’s behavior raises important questions around risk management, liquidity, and scenario analysis. After such an explosive move, the stock’s risk-reward profile is likely to be highly asymmetric, with substantial downside risk if the underlying catalysts prove less durable than the price now implies. At the same time, the conviction implied by market participants willing to chase the stock higher, and the potential visibility of new information or structural changes at the company level, may justify continued tracking and a disciplined approach to position sizing. In the absence of upcoming earnings in the near term, investors will likely need to rely on fundamental research into asset quality, capital allocation, and regulatory risk to decide whether SOC deserves a core or more tactical allocation.

### Wix.com Ltd. (WIX)

Wix emerged as the standout performer in the digital commerce and SMB web presence space, gaining 33.2% over the week and 18.4% over the month. This move sharply outpaced other names in the digital commerce and web infrastructure cohort, including Shopify and GoDaddy, both of which gained 7.8% on the week, and stands in direct contrast to Sea’s 15.2% weekly decline and 13.4% monthly loss. The market appears to be rewarding Wix for its asset-light business model, recurring subscription revenue, and leverage to SMB digitization and e-commerce enablement.

From a thematic perspective, Wix sits at the intersection of several structurally attractive trends, including the proliferation of small and micro-businesses, the shift of services and commerce online, and the increasing importance of performance marketing and data-driven design. The stock’s strong month-to-date performance suggests that the market is gaining confidence in Wix’s ability to sustain growth, improve margins, and convert top-line scale into durable free cash flow generation. For portfolios seeking balanced exposure to the digital commerce ecosystem, Wix offers a complementary profile to Shopify’s broader merchant platform and GoDaddy’s domain-centric model.

### The Trade Desk (TTD)

The Trade Desk delivered a 22.9% weekly gain and a 7.4% one-month increase, leading the adtech and digital media group within the watchlist. This move comes alongside strong weekly performance in related names such as Pinterest, up 16.8%, AppLovin, up 15.5%, Zeta Global, up 11.2%, and LiveRamp, up 8.2%, collectively signaling a broad-based re-rating of digital advertising and marketing technology. The Trade Desk, as a leading independent demand-side platform with deep exposure to connected TV, retail media, and programmatic advertising, stands at the center of this trend.

The re-rating appears to reflect a combination of improving digital ad demand, increased marketer comfort with measurement and attribution in a post-cookie world, and growing confidence that AI-driven optimization will support better return on ad spend. With no imminent earnings catalysts over the next two weeks, investor focus is likely to remain on macro indicators of ad spend, industry commentary, and positioning. For growth-focused portfolios, TTD’s combination of scale, technology leadership, and CTV leverage makes it a core asset for expressing a constructive view on digital media and advertising.

### Samsara Inc. (IOT)

Samsara continued its remarkable run, rising 22.4% on the week and 40.9% over the month, making it one of the best-performing software infrastructure names in the watchlist. The stock has been a prime beneficiary of investor enthusiasm for applied AI in industrial and operational contexts, as Samsara’s platform enables telemetry, fleet management, and data-driven optimization for physical operations. Its strong weekly and monthly performance also stands out within the software infrastructure bucket, where other names like Palantir, Cloudflare, Datadog, and UiPath posted double-digit weekly gains but smaller monthly increases.

In portfolio terms, Samsara offers high-growth, high-beta exposure to the convergence of IoT, AI, and vertical software for physical operations, albeit with valuation and execution risks commensurate with its growth profile. The stock’s sharp appreciation over the past month underscores both the market’s conviction in its long-term potential and the potential vulnerability to sentiment shifts or any indication of decelerating growth. With no near-term earnings catalysts, investors will need to monitor alternative signals such as customer wins, partner announcements, and broader industrial demand trends when evaluating risk-reward.

### Klaviyo, Inc. (KVYO)

Klaviyo posted a 20.5% gain this week and a 1.2% increase over the past month, placing it firmly in the top tier of marketing technology performers, alongside Zeta Global, LiveRamp, and Braze. As a data-driven marketing automation and customer engagement platform, Klaviyo sits at the heart of the first-party data and personalized marketing trend that is becoming increasingly important as cookies deprecate and privacy regulations tighten. The stock’s strong weekly move, after a relatively modest one-month performance, suggests a renewed appetite among investors for marketing tech names that combine robust growth trajectories with improving profitability.

Relative to other martech names in the universe, Klaviyo’s positioning is attractive for portfolios seeking differentiated exposure to the commerce and marketing stack. While Zeta Global and LiveRamp offer strong data activation and identity capabilities, and Braze specializes in customer messaging and engagement, Klaviyo’s strength lies in its deep integration with commerce platforms and its focus on SMB and mid-market merchants. The stock’s recent move may signal growing confidence that it can scale effectively while navigating competition from both point solutions and larger platform vendors.

### Lumentum Holdings Inc. (LITE)

Lumentum was one of the week’s most significant decliners, falling 20.3% on the week, even as it remains up 20.0% over the past month. This pattern suggests that the stock had experienced a strong prior rally and is now undergoing a sharp consolidation, potentially driven by profit-taking, shifts in sentiment on telecom and data center optical investment, or company-specific news. Lumentum’s weakness occurred alongside declines in other hardware and optics names such as Corning, which fell 18.0% on the week but is up 12.4% on the month, and Ciena, which dropped 15.6% weekly yet remains up 16.0% monthly.

For investors, Lumentum’s volatility underscores the sensitivity of optical and telecom-exposed semiconductors to fluctuations in capital spending and to changes in the perceived pace of AI data center build-outs. While longer-term AI infrastructure demand remains a supportive thematic backdrop, short-term swings in ordering patterns, pricing, and customer inventory levels can produce considerable share price volatility. Given the absence of near-term earnings catalysts, Lumentum’s next significant move may be heavily influenced by broader sentiment on AI infrastructure capex and any incremental industry datapoints.

### Corning Incorporated (GLW)

Corning declined 18.0% over the week, even as it is still up 12.4% on a one-month basis. This pattern, similar to Lumentum’s, highlights the extent to which recent gains in specialty materials and glass for display, telecom, and data center applications have come under pressure. Corning’s diversified end-market exposure across consumer electronics, telecom, automotive, and life sciences can provide a buffer over the long term, but in the short term the stock remains sensitive to cyclical swings in demand for display glass, optical fiber, and other components.

From a portfolio standpoint, Corning’s sharp weekly decline introduces both risk and potential opportunity. If the move primarily reflects profit-taking after a strong month, the stock could find support as investors reassess medium-term growth prospects tied to data center build-outs, automotive ADAS penetration, and specialty materials for consumer devices. Conversely, if the decline signals more fundamental concerns about end-market demand or pricing pressure, there may be further downside. Careful monitoring of sector commentary and macro indicators related to electronics and telecom capex is warranted.

### MongoDB, Inc. (MDB)

MongoDB’s 17.7% weekly decline and 19.9% one-month loss make it one of the weakest names in the data and analytics cohort this period, in stark contrast to the strong performance of peers like Datadog, Dynatrace, and Palantir. Investors appear to be reassessing high-valuation growth names where the AI monetization story is still in its early innings and where the path from rapid revenue growth to durable, high-margin cash flow is less certain. MongoDB’s exposure to enterprise database modernization and developer adoption remains a strong secular story, but in the current environment, the market is clearly demanding more evidence of operating leverage and sustainable profitability.

For growth portfolios, MongoDB’s drawdown raises the question of whether the stock now offers an improved entry point relative to peers, or whether it remains exposed to further multiple compression if macro or competitive dynamics soften demand. The relative strength of observability and security peers suggests that investors are prioritizing categories where AI is perceived as both a growth accelerant and a clear margin driver. Without earnings catalysts in the near term, sentiment around MongoDB may hinge on broader spending trends in cloud data platforms and AI workloads.

### Intuit Inc. (INTU)

Intuit gained 17.6% on the week and 8.0% over the month, placing it among the strongest large-cap application software names in the watchlist. The company’s multi-product ecosystem across tax preparation, small-business accounting, and personal finance, along with its growing integration of AI into customer workflows, underpins a durable secular growth thesis. The stock’s performance aligns with broader strength in application software, where several peers including ServiceNow, Constellation Software, and Guidewire also posted double-digit weekly gains.

Intuit’s move likely reflects investor confidence in its ability to deliver consistent revenue growth, expanding margins, and robust free cash flow generation, even against a mixed macro backdrop. Its exposure to small businesses and consumers gives it a degree of cyclicality, but its product breadth and pricing power provide resilience. For portfolios seeking a relatively lower-volatility way to participate in the AI and automation theme within software, Intuit offers a compelling combination of scale, profitability, and innovation.

### Constellation Software Inc. (CSU.TO)

Constellation Software advanced 17.6% on the week and 19.3% over the past month, continuing its long-standing reputation as a compounding serial acquirer of vertical-market software businesses. The stock’s strong performance this period underscores renewed investor appreciation for its highly diversified, cash-generative portfolio and disciplined capital allocation framework. Within the vertical software subgroup, Constellation’s move is complemented by strength in Guidewire, up 16.2% weekly and 27.8% monthly, Manhattan Associates, up 12.6% and 10.1%, and Tyler Technologies, up 5.6% and 9.1%.

For institutional investors, Constellation Software serves as a core holding for gaining broad, diversified exposure to mission-critical vertical-market software across industries. Its ability to consistently deploy capital into accretive acquisitions and then drive operational improvements across acquired assets has historically supported robust total returns. The current period’s outperformance suggests that investors remain comfortable underwriting this playbook, even amidst a dynamic macro and rates environment.

CrowdStrike rose 15.3% on the week and 3.3% over the month, solidifying its position as one of the strongest performers in the cybersecurity cohort. The company’s cloud-native endpoint, identity, and threat intelligence platform has positioned it as a key beneficiary of both secular security spending and AI-enhanced threat detection. CrowdStrike’s strong weekly move is echoed across the cyber group, with Rapid7 up 13.7%, Zscaler up 11.6%, Okta up 11.3%, Palo Alto Networks up 10.8%, and Rubrik up 10.0%.

The stock’s resilience over the month, combined with its robust weekly outperformance, suggests investors are increasingly willing to re-rate security platforms perceived as leaders in cloud and AI-enabled defense. With no near-term earnings catalysts, sentiment is likely to track sector-level news on breaches, regulatory developments, and customer adoption patterns.

### ServiceNow, Inc. (NOW)

ServiceNow advanced 15.1% this week and 11.9% over the past month, reflecting sustained investor enthusiasm for workflow automation and AI-enabled enterprise productivity. The company’s strength is consistent with the broader application software rally and aligns with strong weekly moves in peers like Intuit, Constellation Software, and Workday. ServiceNow’s role as a central platform for IT service management and, increasingly, cross-functional workflow orchestration positions it well as enterprises look to rationalize their software stacks and capture efficiency gains.

The stock’s performance underscores the market’s belief that ServiceNow can maintain elevated growth rates while expanding margins, particularly as it continues to roll out AI-driven capabilities and deeper partner integrations. Palantir gained 14.6% on the week and 12.6% over the month, aligning it with other applied AI and data platform beneficiaries such as Samsara and Datadog. The stock’s performance reflects market conviction in Palantir’s ability to monetize its AI platforms and to translate public-sector and commercial demand into consistent revenue growth. The contrast between Palantir’s positive month-to-date performance and MongoDB’s 19.9% monthly decline highlights investors’ preference for AI narratives backed by visible adoption and strong government or large-enterprise relationships.

For investors, Palantir provides high-beta exposure to AI-enhanced analytics and decision-support systems across defense, intelligence, and commercial customers. Datadog advanced 12.3% on the week and 8.7% over the month, reinforcing its standing as a core holding in observability and cloud infrastructure monitoring. The stock’s outperformance is consistent with the broader strength in software infrastructure and applied AI plays, where Datadog’s integration of AI into anomaly detection and troubleshooting provides tangible value in complex, distributed systems. In contrast to MongoDB’s notable weakness, Datadog’s robust performance suggests that investors are prioritizing categories where AI is both clearly embedded in the product and directly linked to operational efficiency for customers.

In the absence of imminent earnings, Datadog’s near-term price action is likely to track broader sentiment on cloud adoption, enterprise IT budgets, and the intensity of AI-related workloads. Its solid one-month return, coupled with strong weekly performance, indicates that the market is increasingly comfortable with its growth and profitability profile.

### Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL)

Marvell gained 9.7% on the week and 21.5% over the month, distinguishing itself from many other semiconductor names in the watchlist that posted negative weekly returns. As a key supplier into data center, networking, and AI accelerator ecosystems, Marvell has become an important way for investors to gain diversified exposure to AI infrastructure growth beyond the largest GPU vendors. The stock’s outperformance relative to Lumentum, SiTime, Onto Innovation, Teradyne, and several storage names underscores the market’s preference for semiconductors with clear and direct leverage to AI workloads.

For portfolios, Marvell offers a balanced risk-reward profile within semis, benefitting from AI demand tailwinds while still exposed to more traditional networking and storage cycles. The strong monthly performance highlights the degree to which AI enthusiasm has re-rated the stock, implying that investors will closely scrutinize any updates on AI-related revenue mix and margin trajectories.

### Vertiv Holdings Co (VRT)

Vertiv fell 5.1% on the week but remains up 32.4% over the month, reflecting its status as one of the prime beneficiaries of data center and AI infrastructure investment. The weekly pullback likely represents a consolidation after a very strong run, rather than a structural impairment in the thesis. Vertiv’s exposure to power, cooling, and infrastructure management for high-density AI data centers positions it at the heart of the physical build-out required to support AI compute growth.

For investors, the key question is whether the current valuation fully discounts the medium-term AI infrastructure growth opportunity or whether further upside remains as AI deployments scale. The stock’s volatility also suggests that it may be sensitive to any shifts in macro sentiment or commentary on data center capex, making position sizing and risk control particularly important.

CF Industries gained 16.3% on the week and 22.3% over the month, making it a standout within the materials segment of the watchlist. The stock’s strong performance contrasts with weakness in other materials names such as Mosaic, which fell 5.5% weekly and 8.7% monthly, and Kaiser Aluminum, which declined 5.7% weekly and 11.1% monthly. CF’s strength suggests that investors are constructive on fertilizer pricing, agricultural demand, or company-specific execution, even as other commodity-exposed names lag.

For diversified portfolios, CF offers cyclical upside tied to global food demand and fertilizer dynamics, but with risk linked to commodity prices, energy costs, and regional demand patterns. The stock’s outperformance highlights that, even in a market favoring secular growth, there remain selective opportunities within cyclicals where supply-demand fundamentals are favorable.

## Upcoming Catalysts

The near-term catalyst calendar for our watchlist is unusually light, with no earnings releases scheduled over the next two weeks. This absence of company-specific quarterly updates means that price action will likely be driven predominantly by macro data, sector-level news, and idiosyncratic corporate developments rather than the traditional cadence of earnings beats and misses. For many high-beta names that have moved sharply this week and over the past month, including Samsara, Sable Offshore, Wix, The Trade Desk, and CF Industries, the lack of a defined earnings event window shifts the focus toward alternative leading indicators and risk management.

In software and applied AI, where many names have enjoyed strong multi-week rallies, the key near-term catalysts will be macro and industry signals regarding enterprise IT budgets, AI adoption, and cloud consumption trends. Observability, security, and workflow automation leaders such as Datadog, CrowdStrike, ServiceNow, and Intuit are now trading with improved sentiment and higher expectations, which could make them more sensitive to any negative data points or commentary on spending. Conversely, names that have sold off meaningfully, like MongoDB and several semiconductors and storage names, may be poised for relief rallies if macro or sector-level news turns more constructive.

In adtech and digital media, the recent strength in The Trade Desk, Pinterest, AppLovin, Zeta Global, and LiveRamp heightens the importance of tracking indicators of digital ad spend, including any commentary from large platform peers, trends in performance marketing budgets, and macro data on consumer spending. While there are no immediate earnings releases, investors will likely update their views continuously as new datapoints emerge on connected TV adoption, retail media growth, and the impact of AI-driven targeting and optimization solutions.

For energy and materials, including names like Sable Offshore, Valero, CF Industries, Freeport-McMoRan, and Newmont, commodity price trajectories, geopolitical developments, and supply-demand signals will serve as critical catalysts in the absence of earnings. Sable Offshore’s extreme move this week warrants particularly close monitoring for any corporate announcements, regulatory decisions, or analyst actions that could either validate or challenge the recent re-rating. CF Industries’ strong performance, contrasted with weakness in other fertilizers and metals names, also suggests that any incremental information on crop dynamics, planting seasons, or policy changes could have outsized impact on positioning.

In consumer and ecommerce, Wix, Shopify, GoDaddy, Sea, Nike, Home Depot, and other retail-exposed names will be sensitive to incoming consumer sentiment indicators, retail sales data, and any updates from large platform partners or peers. With staples under pressure and discretionary and digital platforms seeing mixed performance, the next macro datapoints related to consumer health could meaningfully influence flows within this cohort. Nike’s 8.3% weekly and 11.2% monthly declines and Home Depot’s 6.0% weekly and 7.6% monthly losses underscore that not all consumer exposures are currently in favor.

Across healthcare and staples, where Elevance, GE HealthCare, Medtronic, Zoetis, and multiple food and beverage names have weakened, macro catalysts related to healthcare policy, reimbursement, input cost pressures, and consumer wage and price dynamics may drive relative performance in the absence of earnings updates. Investors may also look for management commentary at conferences or industry events as interim sources of fundamental insight.

## What To Watch Next Week

Looking ahead to next week, the key priority for a buy-side portfolio anchored in this watchlist is to monitor whether the current rotation into secular growth, software, and applied AI can sustain without the support of near-term earnings catalysts, and whether the derating in semiconductors, storage, and defensives stabilizes or accelerates. The prevailing pattern—strong IGV and software performance, significant gains in applied AI and adtech, and weakness in semis, storage, and consumer staples—could persist if macro sentiment remains balanced and investors continue to prioritize long-duration growth assets.

Within software and AI, continued outperformance of names like Samsara, ServiceNow, CrowdStrike, Intuit, and Constellation Software would confirm that the market is still in a regime favoring quality growth and AI leverage. Any sudden reversals, particularly in high-beta names that have appreciated sharply over the month, could indicate a shift in risk appetite or emerging concerns about valuation stretch. Conversely, stabilization or a bounce in underperformers like MongoDB, Rapid7, and certain DevOps and automation names could signal that the worst of the recent derating is behind them.

In semiconductors and hardware, it will be important to watch whether this week’s laggards—Lumentum, Corning, SiTime, Onto Innovation, Teradyne, Seagate, Western Digital, and Ciena—find support or continue to drift lower. Any improvement in sentiment around data center capex, AI infrastructure demand, or telecom investment could help these names recover, particularly given that several remain up on a one-month basis despite the sharp weekly declines. Alternatively, continued weakness would reinforce the bifurcation between AI-levered semis like Marvell and Vertiv and more traditional hardware exposed to cyclical end markets.

For energy and materials, the central question is whether Sable Offshore’s 74.2% weekly gain marks the start of a durable new regime or an overshoot that will mean-revert. Tracking volume, news flow, and any regulatory or corporate developments will be essential. CF Industries’ continued strength relative to other materials names will also be a focal point, as it may provide clues about the durability of fertilizer and agricultural demand drivers relative to metals and mining exposures like Freeport-McMoRan and Newmont, both of which were under pressure this week.

In adtech and digital media, investors should watch for signs of follow-through in The Trade Desk, Pinterest, AppLovin, Zeta Global, and LiveRamp. Sustained momentum would suggest that the market is increasingly confident in digital ad demand and the monetization potential of AI-driven marketing and measurement. Any sharp reversals would raise questions about whether this week’s gains were driven more by positioning and short covering than by a durable fundamental re-rating.

Finally, in consumer and defensive sectors, it will be important to monitor whether the recent underperformance in staples and healthcare persists, or whether these sectors begin to attract incremental flows as investors reassess valuations and macro risks. Clorox, Unilever, McCormick, Constellation Brands, Mondelez, Elevance, GE HealthCare, Medtronic, and Zoetis all represent potential barometers of risk appetite; stabilization or recovery here could indicate an incremental shift back toward balance between growth and defense.

In sum, next week’s focus should be on the sustainability of the current growth-led, AI-centric leadership; the reaction of underperforming semis, storage, and cyclicals; and the evolution of sentiment toward defensives. With no near-term earnings on deck for the watchlist, macro data and sector-level developments will do the heavy lifting in driving relative and absolute performance, making active monitoring and disciplined risk management paramount.

market_summary:
US equities digested a hotter 4.2% May CPI print and a still-solid May payroll gain of 172k, with unemployment steady at 4.3%, reinforcing the “higher-for-longer” policy narrative even as the S&P 500 and growth benchmarks hold positive year-to-date returns.[30][32][6] VIX slid back below 20 to 19.9, suggesting investors are leaning into risk despite stickier inflation.[20]
Beneath the surface, leadership was narrow and factor dispersion elevated: software, cybersecurity and select AI beneficiaries outperformed, while semis, travel and defensives like staples and health care lagged. Russell small caps retained a strong YTD edge into the June 26 Russell reconstitution, which should amplify flows around cyclicals and higher-beta growth.[28][12] Near term, focus turns to the mid-June FOMC decision, VIX expiry and rebalancing flows as key catalysts for volatility and sector rotation.[31][29][12]
